slot.brief: Show a block released from rest on top of a frictionless incline that compresses a spring at the bottom; ask the maximum compression using conservation of mechanical energy.

stem: A $5\ \text{kg}$ block is released from rest on a frictionless $37^\circ$ incline, $0.50\ \text{m}$ up the slope from an uncompressed spring fixed along it. Find its maximum compression, as shown in the figure. Take $g=10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$, $\sin37^\circ=0.6$, and $k=90\ \text{N m}^{-1}$.

verdicts.working: At maximum compression, the gravitational energy lost over distance 0.50 + x equals the spring energy: 5(10)(0.6)(0.50+x) = (1/2)(90)x². Thus 3x² − 2x − 1 = 0, giving the positive root x = 1.00 m.

working:
$mg\sin37^\circ(0.50+x)=\dfrac12kx^2$ 
$30(0.50+x)=45x^2\Rightarrow 3x^2-2x-1=0$ 
$x=\dfrac{2+\sqrt{16}}{6}=1.00\ \text{m}$

Independent check: At maximum compression, the gravitational energy lost over distance 0.50 + x equals the spring energy: 5(10)(0.6)(0.50+x) = (1/2)(90)x². Thus 3x² − 2x − 1 = 0, giving the positive root x = 1.00 m.
solution:
At maximum compression, the loss in gravitational potential energy equals the spring energy stored:
$$mg\sin37^\circ(0.50+x)=\frac12kx^2$$
$30(0.50+x)=45x^2$, so $3x^2-2x-1=0$. The positive root is $x=1.00\ \text{m}$.

draft.stem: A $5\ \text{kg}$ block is released from rest on a frictionless $37^\circ$ incline, $0.50\ \text{m}$ up the slope from an uncompressed spring fixed along it. Find its maximum compression, as shown in the figure. Take $g=10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$, $\sin37^\circ=0.6$, and $k=90\ \text{N m}^{-1}$.

figure.description: Draw a straight incline descending from upper left to lower right, with a horizontal reference line extending rightward from its lower end. Mark the angle between them as $37^\circ$. Place a rectangular block on the incline above a coil spring. At the lower end, draw a rigid stop perpendicular to the incline; attach the spring to the stop, parallel to the incline and extending uphill, with its free end separated from the block by a visible gap. Add a double-headed dimension arrow parallel to the incline between the downhill face of the block and the spring's free end, labeled $0.50\ \text{m}$. Label the spring $k=90\ \text{N m}^{-1}$ and the incline 'frictionless'.

draft.distractor_notes: A: Omits the gravitational drop during spring compression. B: Uses spring energy $kx^2$ instead of $\dfrac12kx^2$. D: Uses $mg$ rather than the component $mg\sin37^\circ$ along the incline.
